patch.value:
## Problem

`changelog:check` requires each pull request to commit its own entry in the `## Unreleased` section of `CHANGELOG.md`. The tracker is conflict-free: one `.toon` file per item. `CHANGELOG.md` is a single file, and every concurrent PR edits the same section of it. So when one PR merges, every other open PR either fails the check or conflicts:

1. A Dependabot PR without a `CHANGELOG.md` commit fails `changelog:check` with `Drift classification: tracker_changed`. The generated file gains `## Unreleased / ### Dependencies / - Bump …` lines that the committed file does not have.
2. A PR that carries a regeneration commit passes until any sibling merges. The `Unreleased` hunk then conflicts (`DIRTY`), and Dependabot stops rebasing because another author pushed to its branch.

Fleet state on 2026-11-27: **54 Dependabot PRs are stuck**. **24** are `DIRTY` with green checks; each carries one `Regenerate CHANGELOG.md after updating from main` commit that a sibling merge invalidated. **30** are `BLOCKED` on red `changelog:check` / `release-gate` jobs. All 6 failing logs I sampled show only this drift: pm-changelog#379, pm-rl#209, pm-vcs#234, pm-ops#325, pm-slack#224, pm-ts-starter#235 and pm-review#111. Regenerating every branch only buys time: the next merge breaks the rest again. #382, the merged Dependabot subject changing its entry text after merge, is the same class seen from `main`.

## Why the committed Unreleased section is redundant

Pending work is already recorded without conflicts: in pm items, and for dependency updates in commit subjects. Every release path regenerates the file anyway. The shared pm-ops daily release runs `changelog:full` and then `changelog:check` before it commits. That is the same model as changesets or towncrier fragments, and in this model the pm items are the fragments. Only the versioned sections need to be exact in the committed file.

## Expected

- `--check` compares every **versioned** section exactly (heading, date, entries, links), as it does today.
- `--check` treats the `Unreleased` section as pending, whether it is missing, stale or present. Drift there is reported to stderr with its own classification, for example `pending_only`, and exits 0. A strict opt-in flag, for example `--check-pending`, keeps today's exact comparison for callers who want it.
- A PR that only bumps a dependency, or only closes pm items, passes `changelog:check` without touching `CHANGELOG.md`. Merging one such PR never makes another fail or conflict.
- The release path is unchanged. Running `changelog:full` and then `changelog:check` with a pending release version still writes and verifies the new release section exactly. The pm-ops daily release and `release-version-from-package` flows keep working.
- The release note says the default changed and shows the strict flag for opting back in. Consumers need no script change, so a fleet-wide adoption sweep is not needed.

## Acceptance

- A real git fixture with two tags and pending work, both item-driven and Dependabot-subject-driven:
  - the committed file without `Unreleased` passes;
  - with a stale `Unreleased` it passes and prints the advisory;
  - with drift in a versioned section it fails exactly as today;
  - with `--check-pending` and a pending-only drift it fails.
- A fixture modelled on two concurrent branches off the same main: each passes on its own, and the second still passes after the first merges, with no change to `CHANGELOG.md`.
- The SDK, standalone and pm-host invocations agree (existing parity tests).
- Every new behaviour has a test that fails on revert.
changelog:check makes every pull request own the Unreleased section, so concurrent PRs fail or conflict after each merge (54 Dependabot PRs stuck fleet-wide)

value.text: Implemented the comparison in the SDK file check, using the generator's Markdown section boundaries. Both command entry points report pending_only and honor --check-pending. Two branches, both Dependabot squash-subject cases, strict mode, versioned corruption, and non-Git SDK/host parity passed in the fixed fixtures.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Release rehearsal in a disposable full clone: changed package.json from 2026.11.24 to 2026.11.27 and added a synthetic dependency commit. The repository changelog:full wrote '## 2026.11.27 - 2026-11-27' with the 1 to 2 range and PR link. changelog:check passed without writing. Editing the release entry to 1 to 3 failed (exit 1, tracker_changed); regeneration restored SHA-256 8ddf1cef075b69e4c6ac8354d83d835520c714de7ff938e93b38e16648b26528.

value.text: Behavioral reverts in a disposable package: restoring whole-file comparison failed 5 acceptance cases (including both #382 squash cases and concurrent integration); accepting versioned edits failed 3; dropping strict comparison failed 2; omitting the standalone receipt, host advisory or release note each failed 1. Baseline files and tests were retained. Source and test typechecks and docstring lint passed. The optional fleet ESLint comparison found 9 pre-existing diagnostics on both base and head and no new diagnostic.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Reopened work for CodeRabbit review 6087820042. Main is already integrated. Checking whether Markdown-escaped bracket labels bypass the shared release heading identity and covering the same identity in read-only checks, prepend cleanup, promotion, replacement, and structured receipts.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Confirmed the review finding on the previous head with a non-Git tracker and the installed pm host. The governing rule is that all stored Markdown release headings share one label parser for semantic identity. The parser now accepts escaped outer brackets, preserves malformed and literal link-like text, and feeds comparison, prepend cleanup, promotion, replacement, sorting, standalone summaries, structured projections, contract reports, and tagged dependency lookup. The strict check still compares the complete Markdown.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Behavioral revert proof for review 6087820042, in a disposable copy. The four selected tests passed. Restoring only the bracket parser and rebuilding dist made all four fail with assertions, including the installed JSON/TOON host. Restoring only the raw tagged publication lookup failed its projection regression. Restoring only the raw summary formatter failed the summary regression. After restoring and rebuilding, all four passed again. The corpus covers plain and singly/doubly escaped delimiters, optional dates, malformed labels, escaped link-like suffixes, and strict checks.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The round-one package archive matched all 115 files in the checkout, archive, and both consumer installs. Node with npm and Bun each passed nine checks on a fresh non-Git tracker, covering SDK read/strict/write-merge behavior, summary labels, standalone JSON, and installed host JSON/TOON with read-only strict failure. Archive SHA-256 bdeda34613322cf4f39be3f9745d748967243674bb1bd66e1c90d9fb3fa4bf50. The package privacy scan reported zero failures.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Scope correction after the broader suite. The tagged dependency lookup is a separate publication rule. The existing near-match regression requires a canonical heading at the tag, so a semantic label match must never authorize publication. Restored that original comparison and proof script. The added real Git test covers the canonical heading and all four bracket spellings across Markdown, document, and summary generation. The normalized parser remains shared for semantic comparison and summary display.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Final scoped revert proof supersedes the exploratory tagged lookup change. Eight focused tests passed, including all four existing near-match tests. In a disposable copy, the old bracket parser with rebuilt dist failed three regressions, the raw summary fallback failed one, and broadening the canonical publication witness failed the new guard. The four fixed controls passed before and after the mutations. The original publication witness remains in the patch base.

value.text: Review thread PRRT_kwDOSfkApc68zDlg. Main is already included and the follow-up item is open and unclaimed. value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Reproduced the wrong verdict in both directions on the previous head. With a fenced versioned heading under pending text, an older writer changed a release and the modern comparison returned pending_only. A terminal hard break also made a pending-only historical prepend fail. Both modes now scan headings with the selected profile and prepend uses its terminal trim. The SDK, standalone and pm host file checks share this comparator. Historical CLI diagnostics compare full writer output, and the exact canonical tagged publication witness is a separate policy. The two tests cover all five profiles, both fence types, four bracket spellings, read-only strict checks and legacy/current whitespace. In a disposable copy, restoring the default scanner failed only the heading test, and restoring the default trim failed only the whitespace test. Both passed before and after the mutations.
